articles.title: Legal threats loom as margins in Mississippi's Senate race stay razor-thin
articles.summary: Democrats continue to celebrate one of the most lopsided midterm election victories in modern U.S. history, routing their Republican rivals to gain control of the U.S. House, U.S. Senate and statehouses across the country. In the Senate, Democrats flipped seven seats and now hold 54 to the Republican Party's 44. Two seats — nail-biting contests in Alaska and Mississippi — remain undeclared. To do so, Democrats won a series of key battleground contests. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated Mike Rogers in one of the most closely watched races of the midterms. James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, becoming the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate seat in the Lone Star State since 1988.  Annie Andrews beat Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina to flip a Senate seat. In Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson defeated incumbent Sen. Susan Collins, putting an end to her three-decade tenure. Sen. Jon Ossoff comfortably won reelection in Georgia. Other Senate seats to flip to the Democratic Party included Roy Cooper in North Carolina, Sherrod Brown in Ohio, Josh Turek in Iowa and Adam Hamilton in Kansas. In the House, Democrats held 253 House seats to the GOP's 157 as of 2.30 a.m. ET Friday, comfortably passing the majority threshold of 218, with 25 races still to be called. The latest estimates show that the party is on track to win its largest majority since 2008. And there are still seats it could flip, including Colorado's Fourth District, which is held by Republican incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert, a staunch Trump ally, whose race against Democrat Eileen Laubacher remains tight. There were also 36 gubernatorial races , mayoral contests and numerous ballot measures — and plenty of firsts. Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history, while Democrat Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds became the state's first Black governor-elect. El-Sayed will be America's first Muslim senator. At the White House, President Trump signaled he would work with Democrats during his remaining two years in office but said he wouldn't hesitate to use his veto power. The president also acknowledged Wednesday that the Iran war contributed to Republican losses, but defended his decision to pursue the conflict. "If I had to do it again, I'd have to do it again," he said, adding: "You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon." Vice President JD Vance had earlier blamed the scale of GOP losses on the war with Iran. "The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," he wrote in a post on X . "The reason we lost is the war." articles.title: Judge halts construction on Trump’s arch — right after a federal panel approved it
articles.summary: Washington — A federal judge temporarily blocked the Trump administration from beginning construction on President Trump's proposed triumphal arch late Thursday, siding — for now — with a group of Vietnam veterans and the District of Columbia and Virginia, which sued to stop the project. U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan ruled that the government cannot start any "construction-related activity" for 14 days, while further legal proceedings play out. In a 33-page ruling , Chutkan wrote that the plaintiffs are likely to succeed in showing the federal government did not follow required legal processes before moving to build the 250-foot triumphal arch. She also said Virginia and D.C. likely have standing to sue, pointing to "tangible economic harms" caused by traffic problems at the construction site. The ruling came shortly after the National Capital Planning Commission voted Thursday night to approve plans for the arch, giving the final go-ahead for the monument that's set to be constructed between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. The NCPC, which acts as the federal government's planning agency for the region and is stacked with Trump allies, voted 8-4 to greenlight the project after almost 9 hours of public comments from members of Congress, veterans, architects and Washington, D.C., and Virginia residents. Chutkan's order aside, it's unclear how soon construction of the arch could start, though the Justice Department said in a court filing last month that it could begin as soon as Thursday. In a separate filing Wednesday night, the Trump administration said that a construction company "may be — but is not necessarily — arranging off-site preparations for construction mobilization in anticipation of permit approval" at the site. Ahead of the meeting, the NCPC's executive director, Mark Paoletta, recommended approval of the final site and building plans for the structure, which is supposed to celebrate 250 years of American independence. Paoletta, the top lawyer at the Office of Management and Budget, heralded Mr. Trump's "historic vision" for the structure and said it would be the "grandest arch ever built by mankind." But California Rep. Jared Huffman, the top Democrat on the House Natural Resources Committee, said during the hearing that the arch is "illegal" and would "disrupt the solemn connection" between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. "This arch would dishonor America, our ideals, and our laws," Huffman said during remarks to the planning commission, adding that Congress is the appropriate body for debating the proposed monument. One Marine veteran who spoke in opposition to the proposal, Jimi Shaughnessy, said "a dominating arch with a carnival-like atmosphere of tourists, food trucks and buses is abhorrent and insulting to those who gave all and to their families." "Instead of focusing on the issues facing military families, this administration is intent on spending taxpayer dollars to site, plan, and design a monument no one asked for, and are content with bypassing any laws or regulations that may prevent them from breaking ground," he said. The arch itself will be 166 feet tall and topped with "three gilded figures" — a gold, winged female figure flanked by a gold flying eagle on each side — bringing its overall height to 250 feet, according to documents filed with the NCPC. The structure will sit close to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, though the Federal Aviation Administration determined it will pose "no hazard to air navigation," with a "condition for safety lighting that includes a non-standard eternal flame and continuous floodlighting." The arch will also feature an observation deck, and the Trump administration has estimated that it could draw between 2,000 and 22,400 visitors each day. It's expected to take three years to build the arch, which will be located in the center of what is called Memorial Circle, across the Potomac from the Lincoln Memorial. It's unclear how much the project will cost, and who will foot the bill. Mr. Trump said in September that his "Triumphal Arch" would be a "top grade Military Complex" and house drones and sniper ammunition. But the documents from the NCPC do not include the military usage. Lawyers for the Justice Department declined to provide more details about the national security features in an October hearing. The commission received more than 1,300 public comments about the project, most of which were in opposition, it said. The NCPC's approval came as Chutkan weighed how to act. The group of Vietnam War veterans, as well as the Commonwealth of Virginia and the city of Washington, D.C., have filed lawsuits arguing that the Trump administration is acting without congressional authorization and is not complying with the required procedures to construct the monument. In an order Tuesday, Chutkan required the government to provide her notice within one hour of any NCPC vote and a thirty-minute notice to any preparation for construction of the arch to give her time to issue a decision on whether to block construction. The government filed the required notices late Thursday, and Chutkan responded by issuing the temporary restraining order that blocked "construction, excavation, demolition, land-disturbance, utility installation, or roadway-closure activity, or any other construction-related activity" at the site. In a hearing last month, Chutkan said the most important issue for her is whether the Vietnam War veterans had the legal right to sue. Earlier this year, the Supreme Court found that a group of plaintiffs who brought a similar suit to block the White House ballroom construction likely did not have legal standing to challenge the project. In court filings, the Justice Department called the plaintiffs' motions "breathless" and urged Chutkan to follow the Supreme Court's decision in the White House ballroom case, but attorneys for the groups of plaintiffs argued that their legal arguments were different than the ballroom case and urged Chutkan to halt the arch's construction. Two of the plaintiffs, Vietnam veterans Michael Lemmon and Shaun Byrnes, told Chutkan in a hearing last month that the arch construction would impact their experience when visiting graves at Arlington National Cemetery, and said they would be harmed by the arch's size and purpose. In a separate suit brought in late October, Virginia and the District of Columbia sued, and the case was assigned to Chutkan, who had heard arguments the day before from the Vietnam veterans group. The state's attorneys general argued that "as soon as Defendants break ground on this project, they will inflict irreparable harm" on them because "the Arch project will inevitably snarl traffic between the jurisdictions, produce pollution and stormwater runoff in the Potomac, interfere with emergency services, and pose numerous other challenges." articles.title: Kenyan cult leader who ordered followers to starve children to death is jailed for 200 years
articles.summary: Mackenzie was found guilty in October of the murder of 190 children and one adult [Reuters] A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children. Alongside 28 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus". Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie bore the "primary criminal culpability" for ordering his followers to fast to death, in one of the world's deadliest episodes of cult activity. "The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law," the judge added. The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast. The sprawling investigation into the cases shocked Kenya and drew international attention. The court sentenced Mackenzie to 100 years in prison for homicide and another 100 years for offences related to starvation. The sentences within each category will run concurrently, but the two sets will run consecutively, bringing his total prison term to 200 years. Mackenzie also faces separate manslaughter and terrorism charges, which he denies. Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, arguing that the scale and circumstances of the killings warranted the harshest punishment. However, Justice Mochache declined to impose the death penalty, despite ruling that the case met the threshold for its consideration. "Nevertheless, the court declines the invitation to impose the death penalty on any of the victims," she said, adding that capital punishment would eliminate any prospect of rehabilitation and disengagement. The death sentence has not been carried out in Kenya since 1987. Mackenzie was tried alongside 28 accomplices, including guards who enforced his fasting orders and gravediggers who helped conceal the victims' bodies in mass graves. They received varying prison sentences of up to 160 years. Justice Mochache described the killings as "cold and calculated", saying the perpetrators had shown no remorse and had even declared their willingness to fast to death themselves. Before the hearing began on Friday morning, Francis Wanje, who lost eight relatives including two grandchildren in Shakahola forest, told the BBC's Newsday programme that he was "hoping for... a sentence which will match his [Mackenzie's] deeds in the forest". Mackenzie and the co-accused had asked for leniency from the court. Before their conviction on 19 October, they had all pleaded not guilty and repeatedly insisted that nobody was forced to die. More than 400 bodies were dug up in Shakahola forest [AFP via Getty Images] Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece", Justice Mochache said as she delivered her eight-hour judgement last month. Those who opposed Mackenzie's teachings were beaten to death. One of his co-accused said he had told his followers that anyone who "resisted the directive to fast must be forced to go to heaven through kicks and blows". Burials inside the forest where the cult was based were called "weddings" and those who died "were celebrated as having wedded with Jesus" the judge said. The judge found that the deaths arose from an organised system, including religious teachings and directives that compelled followers to follow the deadly fasting. Post-mortem results showed the cause of deaths to be starvation for most victims, while others died from suffocation, strangulation or head injuries. The cause of death could not be determined for some, with their bodies having decomposed, while others died soon after their rescue as they were so emaciated. The Shakahola deaths have shone a spotlight on the lack of oversight of rogue religious activities and how they could have carried on for so long. The gravity of the case prompted President William Ruto to set up a commission of inquiry, although this was later declared unconstitutional. Investigations by the state-funded Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) revealed that local administration and law enforcement officials had repeatedly turned a blind eye to the cult's activities. "We expected at that time the police would take action immediately to go and rescue the other members there, but it didn't happen," said Wanje, who reported the case to the police in March 2023. Wanje said a relative of his in the police force and a former cult participant had managed to save his grandson at the time. The child told the police what had happened and showed them the grave of his siblings. "It was [supposed to be] his last day.. they [would have killed] my grandson." The cult leader had previously been arrested and later released for lack of evidence. Mackenzie established Good News International Ministries in 2003. Over the next 16 years, the church grew in popularity, drawing thousands of followers in its branches across Kenya. The church ran a television station called Times TV which would broadcast his sermons from his church in Malindi. His End Days sermons included conspiracy theories that described education as "evil", healthcare as "against the doctrine" and digital identity cards as "the mark of the devil". The main church shut down in 2019 and Mackenzie moved to Shakahola forest, encouraging his devotees to follow him. While the conclusion of the murder cases may bring a sense of justice for the victims and their families, the convictions only account for 191 victims, while more than 400 bodies were exhumed from the forest. articles.title: Brand faces 'significant' prison sentence after rape and sexual assault conviction
articles.summary: Comedian Russell Brand at Southwark Crown Court in London. Anadolu via Getty Images Russell Brand faces a "significant" prison term after his rape and sexual assault conviction, a judge has said. A jury in London found the British comedian and actor guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault Thursday. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault. The judge told Brand he would be remanded in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday, Nov. 9. "You've been convicted of a number of offenses including rape," judge Joel Bennathan said. "The consequence of that is inevitably a significant custodial term. My current view is that I therefore have to remand you into custody." The actor had been charged on seven counts: three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one count of attempted indecent assault. Following Thursday's verdict, London's Metropolitan Police Service told Yahoo News that Brand, 51, was facing further allegations of rape from two women. "The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations," the force said. Brand has not been charged in relation to these claims. The head of the Met Police, Sir Mark Rowley, has urged any other victims of Brand to contact the police. "There's two more rape allegations that we're looking at. We're encouraging anybody else to come forward if there's any other allegations," he told British media on Friday. He later said that he "wouldn't be surprised if many, many more come forward," adding of the trial, "This shows that powerful people can be brought down so you are safe stepping forward and we will support and try and bring that person to justice." Brand became a household name in the U.K. in the 2000s as a comedian and broadcaster. He went on to star in the movies Get Him to the Greek in 2010 and Arthur the following year. He married singer Katy Perry in October 2010, but Brand filed for divorce in December 2011, citing irreconcilable differences. Their divorce was finalized in July 2012. The claims against Brand were made by six different women, spanning from 1999 to 2009. None of the women knew each other, but all of them came forward to police following a TV documentary and press reports in 2023, in which anonymous allegations were made by other women. Russell Brand was accompanied by his wife, Laura, during the trial. Neil Mockford via Getty Images During the trial, the court heard tearful and forceful testimony from the six complainants, who are all entitled to lifelong anonymity. The convictions included a rape that took place in 2009, involving a victim who went to Brand's home after meeting him at one of his shows. She said she had engaged in consensual sex, but that Brand then raped her and removed a condom in the process. Brand was also convicted of sexually assaulting a woman when he grabbed her breasts at a London bar in 2004. He was also found guilty over an incident in 2009, in which he demanded a woman give him a massage in front of two of his colleagues and then put his head in her groin. A third complaint of sexual assault ended in a guilty verdict when Brand was found guilty of pushing a woman who worked at a radio station up against a wall and forcibly kissing her. Brand denied the charges and said he had never forced anyone to do something against their will. CCTV footage released by the Met Police after the verdict shows Brand being interviewed by police in custody in December 2023. "As I've repeatedly stated publicly and written about extensively, I led a very promiscuous life in the past, which I've spent years openly denouncing," Brand can be seen saying. "I've never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity." He said he did "not recall the names" of the complainants, or meeting them, adding, "However, it's entirely possible that I may have encountered them and we may have engaged in consensual sexual activity or physical contact that's been since reimagined." Following the verdict, the judge told Brand he would be remanded in custody. In a statement, Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy, from the Met Police, said: "Today's verdict is first and foremost a testament to the extraordinary courage, resilience and determination of the women who came forward and reported what happened to them." The statement added: "Brand used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women. "As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement. I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be." Ron Brand, Russell's father, told the BBC he was "shocked" by the verdicts. "I just didn't expect this — it's wrong," he said. "It's devastating." articles.title: More bomb threats target European flights. Officials don't know who's behind them.
articles.summary: A string of bomb threats continued to target flights across Europe on Friday. A Ryanair flight travelling from Rome to Lisbon was placed under a security alert after an anonymous phone call to the control tower at Rome’s Fiumicino Airport warned of a possible explosive device on board, according to reports. The aircraft landed at Lisbon's Humberto Delgado Airport shortly before 8 am. Authorities are investigating the threat, but there has been no confirmation of explosives on board. Meanwhile, the French Prime Minister's office declared that there had been four more bomb alerts concerning "planes flying over French territory" on Friday morning. "The aircrafts landed safely. Security services are conducting inspections", said the PM's office, while adding that "an investigation is underway to determine the source of these alerts, which are affecting the whole of Europe." Concerning the Rome-Lisbon flight, CNN Portugal reported that Portugal's Public Security Police (PSP) received a telephone call from a person described as a "law enforcement officer", warning of a possible explosive device on board. The caller's identity was reportedly verified by the Judicial Police (PJ). When contacted by Euronews, Lisbon Airport referred enquiries to the PSP, which has not yet confirmed the reported incident. Euronews also attempted to contact the PJ but has not received a response. Another bomb alert was reported on a Wizz Air flight travelling from Prague to Rome. The aircraft was diverted to Venice, where it landed. The latest incidents follow a wave of bomb scares that affected at least 25 flights across Europe on Thursday. EU officials have said it is too early to determine whether the incidents are linked. articles.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production after years of poor sales
articles.summary: By Ananya Palyekar, Akanksha Khushi and Nick Carey Nov 6 (Reuters) - Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy ‌pickup trucks that ultimately only sold in just a handful of markets because of its heavy, angular design. Musk said in an X ‌post the production wind-down would enable the automaker to accommodate increased output of its newly launched Cybercab model, which the billionaire has made central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions. While it was not ​immediately clear whether Cybertruck production would be moved to another facility or phased out entirely, the automaker's Austin plant is the only known Tesla facility equipped to manufacture the model's specialized components. In response to a user on X, Musk called the Cybertruck the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and the wind-down the "end of an era". Tesla did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment sent outside regular business hours. The US EV maker only began delivering the Cybertruck to customers in late 2023. ‌According to Kelley Blue Book, the company only sold  20,237 Cybertrucks ⁠in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Before the pickup truck launched, Musk had predicted annual sales of 250,000 units. "It doesn't make sense to keep it going when it's not meeting its targets," said former ⁠Aston Martin CEO Andy Palmer. "Every rational auto guy would say the same." "It will no doubt only be a rounding error on Tesla's balance sheet, but the statistics speak for themselves." 'CYBERTRUCK WON'T GO, CAN'T GO' Right from its unveiling in 2019, the Cybertruck was a controversial choice for Musk. Its angular design was mocked by pickup truck purists and ​safety ​experts predicted it would be hard to gain approval for sale in key markets like ​Europe. The unveiling event itself was marred when Musk tried to ‌prove with a sledgehammer that its windows were shatterproof - only to leave massive cracks in two of them. During Cybertruck's official launch in 2023, Musk touted it as a futuristic competitor to pickup trucks from General Motors and Ford, saying "finally, the future will look like the future". But the vehicle has struggled to meet those expectations. Automotive analyst Automotive analyst Felipe Munoz said that although the Cybertruck has been called a failure because of its poor sales, electric pick-ups from Ford and others have also flopped in the US market. "All of them lost the competition because electric pick ups aren't popular in the US," Munoz said. But Cybertruck's ‌sharp-edged stainless-steel design limited its prospects in markets like Europe where EVs are more popular. Regulatory ​approval was impossible for Europe because of rules there concerning pedestrian impact. "Anywhere where you have ​crash regulation that takes into account pedestrian impact, that Cybertruck won't ​go, can't go," former Aston Martin CEO Palmer said. MUSK'S NEW BET The Cybercab, which has butterfly doors and no steering wheel, ‌pedals or mirrors, is one of Musk's key bets in ​his push to turn Tesla into an ​AI and robotics company rather than just an automaker. Musk has said he sees it as Tesla's main autonomous model supplying a global network of robotaxis. After years of delays to Musk's self-driving targets, Tesla began offering paid rides in a small fleet of Cybercabs in Austin in September. ​However, the automaker still has to answer the US ‌auto safety agency's questions on whether it has properly self-certified Cybercab to demonstrate compliance with federal motor vehicle safety standards. "Cybertruck was an ​incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab," Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill said on X. articles.title: Desert icons collapse as southwestern U.S. gets pummeled with rain and flooding
articles.summary: There are stretches of high desert in northwestern New Mexico where Mother Nature has sculpted otherworldly forms using wind, rain and the passage of time. Hefty planks of rock defy gravity as they balance atop spindly pedestals of clay, while some columns of sandstone take on the appearance of lace, elaborately eroded by the seasons. Tour guide Kialo Winters shares this piece of his homeland on the edge of the Ah-Shi-Sle-Pah Wilderness with visitors regularly. On a recent Friday afternoon, the founder of Navajo Tours USA rounded a bend and found one of the area's most famous features had collapsed. The Alien Throne — or Tsé Bináká Níyol as it's known in his language — was no more. His heart dropped. “It was surreal,” he told The Associated Press. “I had to sort of just pause. A lot of things ran through my head.” The Alien Throne and the nearby King of Wings formation collapsed within weeks of each other, toppled by the very forces of nature that created them. Back-to-back storms destroy homes and hoodoos The southwestern U.S. has endured major rounds of storms over recent weeks, with rain falling on ground already soaked from an especially wet fall. Parts of New Mexico, Colorado, Utah and Arizona have watched rivers crest and floodwaters course through usually dry washes, destroying homes, further saturating the soil and eroding the landscape. The water is receding and cleanup is underway, but officials estimate the damage could stretch into the hundreds of millions of dollars. Winters still is concerned for relatives on the Navajo Nation, where many dirt roads became impassable or were washed away altogether by what he described as a series of massive storm fronts. Experts have estimated that more than 20 trillion gallons (75.7 trillion liters) of rain fell across the Four Corners states and Nevada during late October and early November as tropical moisture was funneled into the region. Condolences shared after the features collapse In early October, the demise of the King of Wings began circulating on social media. Visitors documented the large slab of rock on the ground near the mound of clay on which it once stood. It's not entirely clear when the Alien Throne came down, as poor road conditions kept Winters from visiting for a couple weeks. He had not seen any other posts about the feature's status until he rounded that corner Oct. 30 and saw it in pieces. Social media posts ranged from those who were thankful they were able to see the formations and immortalize them with photographs to those lamenting that they never had the chance. Condolences also were sprinkled in with debates about physics and the fragility of natural wonders. “Gravity. It’s not just a good idea … it’s the law,” one joked. These waypoints won't be forgotten For Winters and other Native Americans from the region, they’re more than just rock formations. They have served as waypoints, guiding ancestors along trade routes for thousands of years, and as connecting threads in stories handed down through generations. “They are culturally relevant to our identity and our stories,” he said, adding that their legacies will be carried on through photographs, illustrations and in the stories people share about their time spent in this stretch of desert. He called on people to let the sites “rest.” So no climbing on what remains, and certainly don't take any pieces home. It's far off the beaten path down a rutted, washboard dirt road. But it's worth it, said Alan Studt of Parma, Ohio, who made his first visit in 2019 and then again last April as part of a 50-day road trip. In looking back through his earlier photographs, he could see the formations were weathering. There were new holes forming in the throne and cracks along the wing's base, making it no surprise they would not last forever. Studt spent hours exploring and photographing the hills and washes during this last trip. He described being drawn in each time he saw a new set of spires in the distance, marveling at the petrified wood along the way and the rainbow of colors in the soils. “It is really so magical to be out there,” he said. articles.title: Hegseth strikes defiant tone in face of impeachment threat
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday dismissed a renewed effort in the House to bring articles of impeachment against him as early as next week. In a video on social media , Hegseth said, “A disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democrat allies, has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly, just like they tried against President Trump twice.” Hegseth was referring to Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., who said Wednesday that he plans to reintroduce articles of impeachment when the House is back in session. Lawmakers are scheduled to return to Washington on Monday. “It’s all about the politics of personal destruction,” Hegseth added. “Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me. You can rest assured of that.” In the more-than-five-minute video, Hegseth only briefly touched on the Iran war — a driving force behind the effort to impeach him, as well as GOP losses in this week’s midterm elections. Massie, who lost his GOP primary after he crossed Trump, urged Trump on Thursday to replace Hegseth while he still has a GOP majority in the Senate. “My Hegseth impeachment resolution is a much gentler version of what’s coming when Dem’s control Congress. They’ll have hearings & trials,” he said on X . “There is one contingency in which I won’t reintroduce the articles of impeachment: Hegseth resigns,” Massie wrote Wednesday . Numerous Democrats have indicated a desire to oust Hegseth since their midterm election wins, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York , who is poised to be the next speaker. Trump said Wednesday that he is not planning to replace Hegseth, and he said Thursday that Hegseth “has done a fantastic job” and “probably has opposition” over the actions he has taken, including purging military leadership. Trump has told some allies he is considering replacing Hegseth, asking them who they think should succeed him, two people familiar with discussions told NBC News this week. He has previously insisted that he was not considering dismissing department heads just days before they were shown the door. Massie tried to force a vote on impeaching Hegseth in September, but his efforts were stunted when House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., sent the House home early. He would need several Republicans to join all Democrats in supporting the impeachment measure for it to succeed. The House has impeached only two Cabinet officials in history — former President Joe Biden’s homeland security secretary, Alejandro Mayorkas, in a partisan vote, and William Belknap, the secretary of war in the 1870s. No Cabinet members have ever been convicted by the Senate. articles.title: Republicans face a crowded agenda and little time before handing Congress to Democrats
articles.summary: Republicans on Capitol Hill are on the clock. They have less than two months left in power before the new, Democrat-led Congress is sworn in and their window of unified control in Washington, D.C., comes to an end. Even as the votes are still being counted, GOP leaders have been putting together plans for what they hope to accomplish before they lose power. “Our job is nowhere close to being finished yet,” House Speaker Mike Johnson reportedly told attendees at a watch party Tuesday night as Democratic victories piled up. The period between the November election and the day in early January when new lawmakers are sworn in, often called the “lame duck” session, can be quite productive as lawmakers move with urgency to get things done while they still can. Some of the most important actions taken by Congress in modern history — the legislative response to the Watergate scandal, the Clinton impeachment, the creation of the Department of Homeland Security and several Supreme Court confirmations — all happened during various lame duck windows. Republicans will have a long list of priorities when Congress reconvenes on Monday, but there are also plenty of potential hurdles that could hinder their progress. Here’s a look at what congressional Republicans want to do and some of the possible curveballs that could derail their plans. What needs to get done Congress will have two “must-pass” items on its agenda when it gets back to work next week: avoiding another government shutdown and passing an annual defense policy bill. Leaders from both parties say they want to get both bills done, but disagreement on the specifics could make for a bumpy and time-consuming process. The government will shut down again on Dec. 12 if Congress doesn’t pass a funding bill to keep it open. After enduring the two longest shutdowns in history over the past two years, neither party appears eager to let another one happen. The big point of disagreement could be timing. Republican leaders are reportedly eyeing a bill that would lock in current spending levels for a full year, but Democrats have an incentive to advocate for a short-term bill that sets them up to enact their own spending priorities once they’re in full control of Congress. Negotiations over the defense budget could be even thornier. The Trump administration has asked Congress for $1.5 trillion in military funding for 2027. Democrats have balked at that number, demanding that the price tag be reduced by hundreds of billions of dollars. Reports suggest that the administration may be open to shrinking its budget request, but landing on a final number that both parties and the president can agree on could prove challenging — particularly if the White House insists on including more funding for the war with Iran. “I don't know what [Trump’s] going to want. I don't know how we're going to figure out the money. So no, I don't have easy answers to that,” Rep. Adam Smith, the top Democrat on the House Armed Services Committee, told Politico on Wednesday. Even if both bills eventually get passed, drawn-out negotiations could eat up precious time and leave little room for Congress to do much else before the end of the year. Republicans’ ‘Last Supper’ In the wake of Tuesday’s losses, some Republican lawmakers have begun advocating for their party to pass one last major budget bill jam-packed with GOP priorities. To do that, they’d need to use the same process they utilized to pass Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill, which creates a pathway to circumvent the Senate filibuster and approve legislation without any Democratic votes. “It’s time to wake up and smell the coffee,” Trump adviser Jason Miller told GOP lawmakers on Wednesday. “You have one job. Get everything on President Trump’s agenda through in the limited days we have.” Before the election, Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno told reporters that he would push for a “giant” spending package during the lame-duck session if the GOP lost both chambers of Congress. “It’ll be the Last Supper,” he said. Actually getting another Republican megabill passed could be a steep challenge. Negotiations over the massive list of complex provisions within the One Big Beautiful Bill took months and consumed big chunks of the congressional calendar. Republicans may also have a numbers problem. Any bill they put forward would need near-unanimous support within their party in both chambers. That includes outgoing senators Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Cornyn of Texas, who have been at odds with the president in the late stages of their time in Congress. Republicans also have other, less ambitious priorities that could be at risk if they dedicate their time and energy to another huge party-line budget bill. One of those priorities is a bipartisan proposal to overhaul the permitting process for energy projects, which would make it easier to build both renewable and fossil fuel infrastructure. There’s also a sweeping slate of reforms to college sports , a number of Trump-nominated judges awaiting confirmation , cryptocurrency legislation and more that could end up on the GOP’s long to-do list. Potential curveballs One of the biggest questions looming over Washington, D.C., since Tuesday is whether any of the Supreme Court’s conservative justices might retire during the lame-duck session. With Democrats pledging to prevent Trump from putting another “right-winger” on the court, this could be a conservative justice’s last chance — potentially for years — to retire with the confidence that their replacement is likely to share their ideology. Neither of the court’s two oldest justices, Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas, has given any indication that they’re considering stepping down — in fact, Alito has reportedly been unequivocal about his plans to stay on the bench. But if one of them did, Republicans would be heavily incentivized to put everything else on the back burner to rush the confirmation of their replacement before Democrats gain the power to block Trump’s nominees for the rest of his presidency. Republicans’ calendar may also get scrambled by some of their own outgoing members. Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican who has been a key voice behind the push for disclosures about the investigation into Jeffrey Epstein, has said he plans to force a second vote on the issue before he leaves Congress. Massie has said he’s also planning to introduce articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who has faced heavy scrutiny for his role in carrying out the war in Iran. Tillis recently told CBS News that Hegseth faces a “reckoning” when Congress reconvenes next week. It’s unclear how much support Massie’s impeachment effort has in the House, but even if it failed, it could consume valuable time Republican leaders would rather spend on other priorities. The same would be true of confirmation hearings for a new defense secretary if reports that Trump is considering firing Hegseth prove to be accurate. articles.title: Moderna Q3营收同比增长29%大超预期，上调全年营收增长指引至15%-25% | 财报见闻
articles.summary: Moderna第三季度营收和盈利双双大幅超出华尔街预期，公司随即将2026年全年营收增长指引从此前的最高10%大幅上调至15%至25%，新品放量与国际市场扩张成为核心驱动力。 公司三季度营收同比增长29%至13.1亿美元，净利润达1.62亿美元，每股收益0.38美元，而分析师此前预期每股亏损1.25美元、营收仅约8.85亿美元。 消息公布后，Moderna股价盘前一度涨约10%，今年以来累计涨幅已逾700%。 CEO Stéphane Bancel在财报发布前接受采访时表示，新品上市和地理布局多元化是三季度强劲表现的主要原因。他指出，公司已获批的次世代新冠mRNA疫苗和流感疫苗正逐步贡献更大收入，同时与英国、加拿大、澳大利亚及墨西哥等国签订的长期战略合作协议为国际市场营收提供了稳定支撑。 新品上市节奏决定短期收入结构 Moderna的次世代新冠mRNA疫苗于2025年5月获得美国FDA批准。 Bancel解释称，由于新冠疫苗合同通常在第一季度完成签订，该产品去年在美国仅完成了"小规模上市"，今年才开始体现"全年影响"。 公司独立流感疫苗mFLUSIVA于今年8月获得美国FDA批准，适用人群为50至64岁成人，65岁及以上人群获加速批准，这也是Moderna全球第五款获批产品。Bancel坦言，由于批准时间晚于年度合同签订周期，该产品在2026至2027流感季将在美国进行"有限上市"，对本财年贡献有限。 此外，mFLUSIVA已在加拿大获批。公司的新冠/流感联合疫苗mCOFLU亦于加拿大获批，并已在欧盟以mCOMBRIAX品牌获批，目前在日本、英国、澳大利亚等市场仍处于审查阶段，美国FDA方面则尚待进一步指导意见后再行申报。 国际市场与政府长期合作构成营收支柱 三季度国际市场营收为5.33亿美元，美国市场营收为7.80亿美元，国际收入贡献占比约40%。公司预计2026年全年约半数营收来自美国，另一半来自国际市场。 Moderna在国际市场的战略布局持续推进。公司在三季度执行了与英国、加拿大和澳大利亚政府签订的长期战略合作协议，并于9月与墨西哥一家本地制造商签署了五年期新冠疫苗合作协议，旨在强化经常性收入来源并扩大国际市场覆盖。 在财务层面，公司三季度末现金及投资余额升至80亿美元，较二季度末的69亿美元有所提升，主要得益于9月完成的总额约30亿美元可转换优先票据发行，扣除购买对冲上限期权等相关费用后净融资约26亿美元。公司将2026年末现金及投资预期从此前的47亿至52亿美元大幅上调至81亿至83亿美元。 个性化癌症疫苗数据积极，监管申报准备推进 Moderna与默克（Merck）于10月在欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）年会上公布了个性化癌症疫苗intismeran autogene（mRNA-4157）的积极三期临床数据。在已切除高风险黑色素瘤患者中，intismeran联合默克免疫治疗药物KEYTRUDA（pembrolizumab）与单用KEYTRUDA相比，可将复发或死亡风险降低42%（HR=0.58），将远处转移或死亡风险降低38%（HR=0.62）。在预设的敏感性分析中，完成intismeran免疫接种方案六个月后，联合治疗组复发或死亡风险进一步降低58%。 数据公布前数日，部分试验结果遭社交媒体泄露，引发股价短期大幅波动。Bancel称这一市场反应"令人意外"，并表示长期投资者和分析师在深入研究完整数据后给出了积极评价，临床医生也对数据结果印象深刻，并表达了在实际诊疗中使用该产品的意愿。目前，两家公司正推进监管申报准备工作，潜在商业化上市有待监管批准。 成本压缩与管线推进并行 三季度研发费用同比下降27%至5.83亿美元，主要源于部分传染病后期研究完成并进入收尾阶段，以及公司持续推进全面降本。全年研发费用预期从此前约29亿美元下调至约27亿美元，全年运营支出整体较前次预期改善约2亿美元。 诺如病毒疫苗（mRNA-1403）方面，三期临床中期分析未能达到早期成功的统计标准，公司表示本季不再启动额外受试者队列，将与卫生监管机构协商下一步推进路径。 罕见病领域，丙酸血症疗法（mRNA-3927）的注册研究已完成目标入组，关键数据有望于2026年内公布。甲基丙二酸血症疗法（mRNA-3705）的关键研究启动决策则将推迟至丙酸血症数据读出后再行评估。 公司定于11月12日举办分析师日活动，届时有望就管线进展和中长期战略提供更多细节。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: IT技术太烂，日本正在被黑客们当怪刷
articles.summary: “ 黑日本公司，已经成一项运动了” 前几天，Reddit 上有个老哥发了这么一句感慨。起因是他刷到一页日本新闻，全都是“XX 公司被黑客攻击，数据可能泄露”。 比如 10 月 5 号，连锁烤肉店“烧肉 King”道歉，说自家 App 有 1078 万多条会员信息可能泄漏； 四天后，订机票酒店的 Skyticket 立马跟上，说俺也有 1464 万条信息可能泄露； 同一天，二手书巨头 Bookoff 也说可能有 643 万条数据外泄。 短短 4 天，就有三家公司 3000 万条会员信息存在泄露风险。 而这，还只是冰山一角。 根据时事通信社和安全厂商 CS2 汇总，从 9 月 25 日到 10 月 9 日，日本已有十几家知名企业和机构宣布被黑客入侵、数据疑似泄露。 好好好，现在鞠躬道歉都得组团了。。。 面对这场声势浩大的“黑客运动”，日本官房长官只能表示还不清楚事件之间有无关联；而警察厅的攻击手法调查，据说要到 2027 年 3 月才出结果。 不是哥们儿，真到那会纪录片都出第二季了吧。 看到这你可能好奇，怎么突然这么一大波黑客入侵企业爆发呢？ 要世超暴论，背后肯定是 AI 。 虽然官方还没调查出来黑客有没有用 AI，但趋势已经很明显了： 日本警方之前就抓过好几个拿 ChatGPT 入侵日企的青少年；10 月 14 日日本安全公司 Scutum 也发文实锤，至少有 3 个 IP 正在用 AI Agent 攻击日本企业网站，其中一个 IP 在 8 小时内丝滑切换了十几种黑客工具。 可问题又来了，AI 黑客满世界都是，怎么偏偏逮着日本企业往死里薅呢？ 不好意思，这锅一半都得日本人自己背。 首先，很多日本企业的 IT 基础设施老旧，安全管理也长期落后。 9 月 28 日，漫画界扛把子集英社宣布被黑，原因是旗下博主管理系统的 CMS 配置错误。CMS 就是网站的内容后台，它留了个专门口子给程序对接用，本来要先核对身份再放行，结果设置出错了，黑客绕过检查给自己开了个管理员级别的账号。 就好比写字楼的门禁办卡机设置错了，本来只有物业能办卡，结果路人站过去刷一下，就给自己办了张全楼通行卡。 日本警察厅统计，今年上半年就有 123 起勒索软件案，创下有统计以来的最高纪录，而一半受害者的突破口都是 VPN 设备。 说实话，如果你用过日本网站，对这个结果不会意外。 那股扑面而来的千禧年气息，总能让人恍惚间以为穿越了回二十年前。 说直白点就是： 企业的 IT 技术和意识，非常落后。。。 日本气象厅官网 有网友吐槽 2026 年了，日本很多网站的密码还不准用 *、!、: 等特殊字符，长度限制在 8 到 12 位，生怕黑客暴力破解时算力不够用； 还有人说有些大公司的密码和用户名一模一样，而且至今迷恋一种“PPAP”古老仪式，就是先给你发一封加密 ZIP 压缩包邮件，紧接着再发第二封邮件，把解压密码明文发给你。 这 TM 和把钥匙压在门口脚垫下，再贴张纸条“钥匙在脚垫下”有什么区别啊啊？ 也有人说，某家制造业公司死活不肯升级 ERP 系统（企业管理软件），让员工在虚拟机里接着用 Windows 7，但 Win7 早在 2020 年就停止安全更新了啊。。。 看到这你可能会觉得困惑：日本不是科技强国吗？ 日本强的是制造业，像汽车、相机、游戏机都能卖到全球； 但软件系统，尤其企业自己内部用的 IT 系统，几乎都交给了外包公司。 之前日本信息处理推进机构发过一组白皮书。 在美国，65.4% 的 IT 人才受雇于各大用户企业（比如银行、零售商、制造厂自己养的技术团队），只有 34.6% 在外包 IT 公司。 但日本完全是反过来的。 2015 年，日本有 72% 的 IT 人员在外包 IT 公司；到了 2020 年，这个比例是 73.6%，还能涨？！ 这意味着：绝大多数日本传统大企业，内部几乎没有研发和运维能力。 这种信息不对称和繁琐的对接流程，造成企业在 IT 维护方面极其落后，几乎就是“能用就别动啦”。 那这种大环境下，奇葩的密码规则和配置错误就不奇怪了。 更关键的是，这种全员外包的模式，在供应链攻击面前就是一个超级连环雷：只要一家底层外包商被黑客攻破，那它身上的大企业客户就会像多米诺骨牌一样，一个接一个倒。 比如 10 月 5 日到 6 日，大和证券、西铁城前后脚宣布数据可能泄露，就是因为给他们提供客服系统的同一家外包商 被端了。 卡拉 OK 巨头 Big Echo 872 万条信息可能泄露，也是由于外包商一名员工的电脑中了病毒。 按理说日本企业 IT 这么老旧、安全管理这么落后，早该出事了，为啥偏偏是现在才集中爆雷呢？ 世超觉得是 AI 模型的能力又上升了一个台阶。 以前，黑客们压根没那么多精力去一家家企业破解，哥们费老劲肯定是想吃点好的吧？很多企业就这么靠“性价比低”撑到了今天。 但 AI 一来，谁跟你俩性价比？黑客多打一家的边际成本几乎为零。 而且，过去那些扫描出漏洞之后的难题，什么利用漏洞，黑入后找哪些数据呀、工具不管用该换哪个，都得黑客坐在电脑前一步步手动操作，一个人一天打不了几家。 但现在这些步骤也能交给 AI Agent 了，AI 可以 24 小时一家接一家试下去。 针对日本电商 SQL 注入攻击，攻击源 IP 数量两月暴涨到 16 倍 其次， AI 也把当黑客的门槛砍没了。 以前当黑客要懂底层架构、懂汇编、懂漏洞挖掘；现在你只需要懂怎么跟 AI 聊天，就能拥有一个黑客的身份。 前面说过，日本警方已经抓了不少拿 AI 作案的赛博未成年。 2025 年 2 月，东京警视厅逮捕了 3 名只有 14 到 16 岁的初高中生。他们用 AI 写了个非法登录程序，登进别人的乐天移动账号，疯狂开通手机卡再转手倒卖。 12 月，日本连锁网咖“快活CLUB”宣布 729 万名会员信息泄露，后来才发现始作俑者是个 17 岁的大阪男高中生，用 ChatGPT 改进了作案程序，作案群里甚至还有个小学六年级的小孩哥。 嗯，AI 实现了科技平权也实现了犯罪平权。 以前你是菜鸡，你只能在键盘上扣 666；现在你是菜鸡，AI 手把手教你写脚本进局子。 一边是 AI 技术的迅速发展，一边是稀烂的 IT 基础设施。 日本，就这么成了黑客的新手村。 虽然这故事听起来像是个日本限定笑话，但这场运动肯定不会只停留在日本。 大模型行业的进化速度还是太快了： 像 10 月初冲上 GitHub 热榜第一的逆向工具 REA，有网友拿它破译了小区门禁 App，还有人半小时就逆向了马桶小程序的蓝牙协议。 当普通人花半小时就能破解软件和协议，那以后能不能破解工厂流水线控制端、老家医院的老系统呢？ 一旦某天 AI 黑客们在新手村刷满了经验，那下一张被刷爆的地图，就只会是这世上任何一个还心存侥幸、以为没人会注意到的薄弱角落。 毕竟从来没有嫌肉少的猎人，只有还没来得及躲藏的猎物。 来源： 差评X.PIN 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 中选后华尔街集体看多美股，结果一天就被打脸！
articles.summary: 美国中期选举落地后，华尔街主要交易机构集体看多美股，却在短短一天内遭遇市场的猛烈反击。 选举结果出炉后，摩根大通、Citadel Securities、瑞银等机构相继向客户发出买入信号，核心逻辑高度一致：选前机构持仓已大幅压缩、不确定性消散将推动资金回流，美股年底前阻力最小的方向是向上。周三，标普500指数单日涨近2%，道琼斯指数涨逾3%，市场走势一度印证了这一判断。然而仅隔一日，围绕人工智能交易的焦虑情绪骤然升温，纳斯达克100指数单日蒸发2.3万亿美元市值，标普500指数暴跌4.4%，所有板块无一幸免。 这一逆转令华尔街交易台措手不及。 高盛美洲股票执行服务主管John Flood在客户报告中写道，周三是高盛股票交易台今年最繁忙的交易日之一，而周四则是"截然相反"——"我们的电话被问询信息炸爆，但遗憾的是我们也看不清方向。"他表示，长线投资者再度"陷入僵局"。 选前集体看多，逻辑高度一致 中期选举结果出炉前后，华尔街主要交易机构几乎异口同声地向客户发出看多信号，核心依据在于选前仓位已极度压缩、反弹燃料充足。 Citadel Securities的Scott Rubner在客户报告中写道："随着选举结束、波动率有望正常化，投资者重建风险敞口的空间相当充裕。随着不确定性消退、市场最大买家陆续回归，我们认为美股年底前阻力最小的方向是向上。"Citadel Securities数据显示，系统性趋势追踪策略当前美股净持仓约为负3.3个标准差，处于2018年以来历史第10百分位，一旦市场持续站稳关键技术位，趋势追踪策略有望触发系统性补仓。 瑞银的Davide Montoni同样认为，选举可能成为科技股震荡后的上行催化剂。"超大规模云计算企业的财报显然未能给投资者带来定心丸，但跨过选举这道坎，或许能成为触发年底轧空行情的关键。"摩根大通美国市场情报团队则维持战术看多立场，认为10月科技股的大幅回调已为近期反弹创造了机会，并建议采取科技股与周期股"哑铃策略"。 支撑这一判断的数据同样充分：对冲基金在选前持续削减美股敞口，空头头寸一度接近五年高位；散户自10月5日以来连续22个交易日净买入美股，累计买入近330亿美元；企业回购窗口随财报季结束大规模重开，预计11月9日前可回购市值比例将升至85%。 一日之内，多头判断全面落空 然而，选举的落地并未消除压制市场的核心矛盾。 据彭博报道，周四，围绕人工智能投资回报与算力建设成本的担忧骤然爆发，纳斯达克100指数单日蒸发2.3万亿美元，标普500指数下跌4.4%，所有板块全线收跌。高盛的John Flood指出，此前因选举不确定性而大幅削减仓位的投资者，被周三的反弹打了个措手不及；对冲基金随即开始抛售前一日刚刚买入的AI超大规模云计算股票，长线投资者则再度陷入观望。 在此之前，巴克莱全球股票战术策略主管Alex Altmann是华尔街主要交易台中为数不多的怀疑者之一。他此前警告称，中期选举不太可能成为市场期待的"清场事件"——压制股市的最大因素，如AI的投资回报前景以及算力建设的融资成本，并不会因选举结果而得到解决。 系统性卖压叠加，跌幅超出预期 此次暴跌的烈度，在很大程度上被系统性策略的机械卖出所放大。 据彭博报道，巴克莱股票战术策略模型显示，波动率控制基金可能在单日内削减约30个百分点的股票敞口，这是自新冠疫情引发市场动荡以来最大规模的单日调仓之一，对应未来24至48小时内约1350亿美元的美股期货抛售。Alex Altmann表示："我们预计这一趋势明日将延续，因为去杠杆将蔓延至散户和长线投资者渠道。" ETF再平衡进一步加剧了抛压。巴克莱指出，周四预计是有史以来规模最大的杠杆ETF卖出再平衡日。 此前被视为市场下跌时重要买盘来源的散户投资者，这一次也选择了撤退。据Vanda Research数据，截至周四纽约时间下午3时，散户已净卖出3.38亿美元的个股，有望创下新冠疫情以来最大单日净卖出纪录。 短期波折，多头逻辑尚未终结 尽管遭遇重挫，华尔街的看多判断并未就此宣告终结。 据周五纽约时间早间6时25分，标普500期货上涨0.3%，纳斯达克100期货跳涨1.5%，显示市场情绪有所企稳。正如彭博所指出的，单日的大幅波动并不足以改变市场趋势，此前各交易台的看多观点或许仍将在未来某个时点兑现。 但这场集体"打脸"事件，深刻揭示了预判股市方向的难度——即便是华尔街最顶尖的专业机构，在面对AI估值重构这一结构性变量时，同样难以做到未卜先知。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 法国财政危机、欧盟政治重组与地缘冲突交织，欧洲或迎2027年系统性考验
articles.summary: 法国财政持续恶化正将欧盟推向一场系统性压力测试。预算赤字攀升、债务规模扩大、政治动荡加剧，三重压力叠加之下，法国主权债务风险的溢出效应已引发市场对欧元区整体稳定性的深层忧虑。 法国国民议会日前以全票否决了政府提出的预算案，导致债券市场进一步承压。此前公布的数据显示， 法国政府预算赤字已升至5.1%，为近四分之一世纪以来的最差水平；公共债务规模更突破GDP的115%。信用评级机构惠誉（Fitch）随后将法国评级展望由"稳定"下调至"负面"。 这一系列连锁反应引发外界对法国是否迫近主权违约边缘的担忧，并直接波及外界对欧元区整体韧性的判断。分析人士指出，若危机失控，欧洲中央银行的救助将成为防止主权违约的唯一可行选项，但这一路径对德国构成沉重负担，在德国经济自身已深陷困境的背景下，其可行性存疑。 违约风险：欧央行救助的两难困境 市场对法国财政路径的担忧，已不仅停留于技术层面。允许法国这一体量的经济体发生主权违约，将在多重压力下严重动摇国际社会对欧元的信心。然而，阻止这一局面发生的唯一手段，或许只剩下欧央行的直接救助。 问题在于，这一选项的代价高度集中。欧央行救助将对德国造成巨大财政压力，并直接冲击德国国内储户利益。 尽管2010年、2012年和2015年三度救助希腊被视为稳定国际市场、捍卫欧元区存续的必要之举，但对法国实施同等规模救助，所需动员的资源和政治意愿可能远超各方承受极限。 雪上加霜的是，德国经济自身也已在多重压力下持续承压多年。绿色监管政策对工业部门造成的结构性冲击，叠加俄乌战争、美以与伊朗冲突以及霍尔木兹海峡动荡所带来的地缘政治风险，令德国经济元气大伤，其充当"最后救助者"的能力受到严峻质疑。 政治真空：马克龙时代的"旋转门"困境 法国的困境并非单纯的财政问题，其政治体系同样陷入深度失灵。自2022年以来，马克龙总统任期内已先后更换五位总理，折射出传统政治架构在应对多重危机时的结构性疲态。 更深层的张力在于，法国当前正面临大规模抗议、骚乱和社会秩序失序，社会结构的撕裂已肉眼可见。 明年5月的法国总统大选将是关键变量，Marine Le Pen的胜选概率正在上升。她目前承诺将在2032年前把法国公共支出压缩至GDP的50%以下。然而，即便是温和的财政整固举措，在法国历史上也每每引发激烈抵制，使得任何政治派别都难以推行实质性改革。 这种政治失能并非法国独有。分析人士认为，当前西方多国政府普遍陷入类似的"旋转门困境"——即便是在意大利这样已由民粹政党执政的国家，Giorgia Meloni政府实际上也并未对战后主流共识带来实质性突破。这意味着，当前欧盟各国的民族主义政治浪潮，或许尚未触及其最终形态，若现有建制持续失效，更强硬的政治选项浮出水面的概率将进一步上升。 多节点承压：波兰危机与中欧板块的战略再定位 在法国财政风险之外，欧盟内部的政治断层线正在多点延伸。波兰当前正经历的政治与宪法危机，将成为欧盟制度韧性的另一重要压力测试。 亲欧派总理Donald Tusk与以总统Karol Nawrocki为核心的民族主义反对派之间的权力角力，将为观察欧盟内部全球主义与民族主义力量对比提供重要参照。波兰的战略意涵日益突出：在欧盟经济普遍低迷的背景下，波兰经济近年来实现了显著增长； 其央行近年持续推进黄金储备积累，当前持有量已逾630吨，跻身全球前十。 从更宏观的视角来看，波兰、捷克、斯洛伐克和匈牙利所构成的中欧板块，有潜力逐步演化为欧洲内部一个更具独立性的区域权力单元。这一进程的走向，同样与俄乌战争的最终结果深度绑定——后者将从根本上重塑欧洲大陆的整体战略格局。 2027年：多重危机汇流的系统性拷问 综合来看，2026年埋下的诸多隐患，可能在2027年形成危机共振。法国财政崩塌风险、欧盟内部政治重组、地缘冲突余波与能源格局重塑，多条危机主线存在并发交织的可能性。 各国政府应对"多重危机同步叠加"的能力，将成为衡量欧盟等超国家权力结构是否具备持久生命力的关键指标。这些机构诞生于二战后截然不同的历史语境，其制度弹性能否经受当前这一历史转折期的考验，市场正在寻找答案。对投资者而言，欧元资产的风险溢价重定价，或许才刚刚开始。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 对标2000 与 2008：本轮 4.1 万亿AI 债务裂痕有多深？
articles.summary: 近期，随着美股科技巨头财报陆续披露，市场担忧的焦点已从此前的AI盈利预期与资本开支回报，进一步转向AI债务融资能力。随着AI产业继续以史无前例的速度扩张，AI巨头资产负债表所体现的债务水平仅是其债务总额的冰山一角；真正隐藏在水面之下的，是庞大且盘根错节的表外债务。 截至目前，包括Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊、SpaceX、英伟达、博通及甲骨文在内的8家AI综合体，其表外承诺总额已攀升至4.11万亿美元。这一数字较Q2末3.12万亿美元激增近万亿美元。其中，长期采购承诺约2.25万亿美元，尚未开始的租赁约1.39万亿美元，担保及备用信贷约2730亿美元。 当前AI综合体在资产负债表中实际报告的金融债务与租赁负债合计约为1万亿美元。这意味着AI综合体每1美元表内债务和租赁背后，对应超过4美元的表外承诺。 现阶段科技巨头CDS持续飙升，甲骨文5年期CDS一度触及343个基点的历史峰值，高评级科技债券收益率升至两位数，AI融资环境显著恶化。面对4.1万亿美元表外承诺与日益收紧的信贷环境，这一局面令人回想起2008年金融危机前对次贷规模的低估及其灾难性后果。若市场持续低估AI表外承诺所蕴含的结构性债务矛盾，是否也将低估由此衍生的系统性风险？ 两轮历史大对标：AI债务与2008次贷、2000互联网泡沫

articles.title: 旗舰配置下沉，车企争抢家庭SUV市场
articles.summary: 作者 | 周智宇 家庭SUV市场的上新持续提速。 9月以来，小鹏G9L、启境GX7、大众ID.ERA 8X及改款理想i6等接连入场，部分产品的上市优惠起价已接近20万元。11月5日，智己LS8 NEO纯电以23.98万元起的权益价加入竞争，将全线控底盘列为全系标配。 这轮密集投放背后，是车企对增长机会的集中争夺。乘用车市场承压，20万—30万元SUV却仍在前三季度保持增长，成为车企争取家庭用户的重要市场。但需求增长与新车增加并不同步，更多产品进入，也意味着后来者必须从已有选择中争取用户。 旗舰技术和配置因此被带入更低价位。平台复用、集团产业资源和专业供应商合作，为车企提供了下放技术的条件，也让消费者能以相近预算比较更多产品。一项过去足以拉开差距的配置，如今要和空间、舒适性及整车价格一起接受挑选。车企需要保留自己的技术特点，又难以在家庭用户看重的其他方面留下短板。 智己汽车品牌用户高级总监焦樵在11月5日晚间的判断是，今年市场承压，明年仍有较大压力，而消费者喜欢的产品越来越多，已经有些“挑花眼”。 随着旗舰技术加速下沉，家庭SUV的竞争还将加剧。车企要把新品带来的关注转化为稳定的市场份额，既要持续更新产品，也要靠规模和效率支撑投入。 技术长板之外 “把整体销量和市场份额做上去。”谈到连续投放新车的目标时，焦樵给出了这一回答。他介绍，全新一代LS6纯电首月交付达到8000辆，超过公司预期；接下来的LS8，则承担着进一步扩大市场覆盖的期待。 围绕这一目标，智己选择将全线控底盘全系标配：此前的LS6覆盖20万元级，LS8则进入25万元级家庭SUV市场。这意味着，技术下沉从入门版本就开始参与竞争，相应投入也要在主流价位里消化。 智己汽车CTO项娇对华尔街见闻解释，能够这样做，既依赖自研，也依赖上汽的产业体系。他介绍，上汽从2018年开始相关前瞻研究，至今已有八年；线控底盘在软件、安全等方面的开发量，是传统转向系统的数倍，甚至十倍。较长的技术积累和自有产业体系，是他所强调的成本控制条件。 这也是智己争取规模的一项筹码：把集团长期投入形成的能力，连续用于面向不同价位的产品。 在电池与辅助驾驶上，智己选择与宁德时代、Momenta等专业供应商合作。项娇用“专业的事交给专业的人”解释这种分工。由此看，智己的扩量思路包含两部分：依靠自身及集团积累建立技术特点，同时通过外部合作形成整车所需的能力。 但技术下沉并不意味着家庭用户会降低其他要求。焦樵强调，不能因为底盘用得好、电池用得贵，就在其他配置上妥协。他将“冰箱、彩电、大沙发”视为基本配置，同时也观察到，市场上的一些功能越来越相似，技术出现同质化。 两种判断放在一起，呈现出智己面对的现实：品牌需要用底盘等技术拉开差异，家庭SUV市场又要求它提供一套完整的空间与舒适体验。消费者最终比较的是同一价格下整车能提供什么，单项技术的投入，并不能替代对其他需求的满足。 用户的选择，还可能修正车企对产品的预判。 “预售时选择大六座版本的用户比我们想象得多得多，我比较意外。”焦樵说，此前发布会主要讲大五座，六座升级包只是最后提及，正式上市时则增加了对六座的介绍。他认为，增加2万元能够获得第三排座椅及其他配置，是吸引这部分用户的原因。 智己没有披露具体预售占比，但这一反馈说明，企业以大五座定义产品，用户却可能把它当作一个可在五座、六座之间选择的家庭购车方案。 旗舰下沉后的竞争 车企集中进入这个市场，有需求基础，也有大盘压力。 乘联分会周度分析的初步统计显示，10月国内乘用车零售169.3万辆，同比下降25%。而根据其9月深度分析报告，前三季度按车型起步指导价划分的20万—30万元SUV零售达到147万辆，同比增长2.8%，同期SUV整体零售下降12.5%。这个涵盖不同动力、座位布局的价格带，仍保持着增长。 理想i6已经验证了其中的规模机会。根据理想汽车公布的交付数据，今年3月至5月，i6连续三个月交付超过2万辆。理想汽车产品线负责人刘杰在10月提到，i6是理想全系车型中首次购车用户最多的产品，吸引新用户是其定价的重要考虑。 对智己而言，这意味着LS8有机会接触此前未购买过自己产品的家庭，也意味着它需要面对已经形成销量规模的竞争者。新用户可以来自首次购车、换购，也可能来自对其他品牌的重新选择。每家车企增加一款车型，并不会让整个市场同步增加一份需求。 LS8的六座反馈又扩大了竞争的范围。用户会把座位数、装载空间、配置和价差放在一起权衡，五座与六座并不是彼此隔离的市场。大五座车型争取增长时，也可能与周边价位的六座车型争取同一批消费者。 技术和配置的下沉，也有不止一条路径。 小鹏汽车产品矩阵总经理吴安飞在G9L上市后表示，G9L与GX在三年多前便开始同源开发，共用多项底层技术，G9L则重新设计上车身、适配五座需求。蔚来创始人、董事长兼CEO李斌此前也表示，乐道L80与L90从产品定义之初就在同一平台规划，研发效率和成本一并考虑。 另一条路径来自专业供应商。启境GX7 9月23日上市，限时权益价22.99万元起，采用华为乾崑多项技术方案，并全系搭载宁德时代电池； 10月12日上市的大众ID.ERA 8X，上市限时权益价20.68万元起，也搭载了Momenta辅助驾驶方案。 宁德时代、Momenta同样出现在智己的合作体系中。车企内部的平台复用，让研发成果服务更多车型；专业供应商的合作，则让相应技术和部件进入不同品牌。旗舰配置能够向更低价位覆盖，背后既有整车企业的积累，也有供应体系的支持。 不同品牌采用同一家供应商，就要做出差异化的具体方案和体验；更具体的差异仍需要通过整车集成、标定和长期使用表现体现。 被问到全线控底盘究竟领先行业多久时，项娇没有给出数字。他说，“我们无法判断究竟能让别人落后多少年”，也希望行业一起推动数字底盘发展。 这意味着，智己需要持续建立差异，而不能只依靠某项技术在上市时的领先位置。焦樵所强调的“其他配置不能妥协”，也会让技术更新与家庭需求长期并行。 持续满足这些要求，也会受到经营条件的约束。刘杰此前提到，i6在常州工厂已经满产，老款车型毛利很薄。 规模已经形成的产品，也未必有充足余地消化下一轮升级投入。对车企而言，配置下放能否长期持续，仍要依靠研发复用、制造效率和供应链协同来支撑。 二十多万元的家庭SUV仍有增量，技术变革也给了后来者改写竞争格局的机会。 风险提示及免责条款
